title: latency-versus-econ-gpu-sensitivity-notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick working notes tying latency SLOs to per-token economics and perf/W when choosing instance mix (A10 / L4 / A100 / H100). This is an informal runbook for product + infra to decide defaults for: persistent chat routes (low p95 need), batch-heavy long-gen, and bursty traffic.

Summary (quick takeaways):
- L4 looks like the best perf/W and best $/token for low-latency, low-batch chat scenarios (assuming our L4 configs and q4/int8 quant).
- A100/H100 provide higher absolute throughput (tokens/s) and are attractive when you can fill big batches or have many concurrent streams; their $/token advantage only shows up at high sustained utilization.
- A10 is the cost-minimal option for extremely low-utilization single-stream workloads (cheaper hourly cost), but its perf/W and absolute throughput make it poor for scale or high-concurrency.
- Important caveat: these numbers are synthetic; power measurement, model variants, quantization levels and kernel sets will change outcomes.

Assumptions used for quick math (document these in the canonical sheet):
- Instance (hourly) costs (internal rack/cloud blended estimates): A10 = $0.40/hr, L4 = $0.65/hr, A100 = $2.80/hr, H100 = $3.50/hr.
- TDP / typical sustained draw used for perf/W calc: A10 = 150W, L4 = 75W, A100 = 400W, H100 = 700W. (Measure later.)
- Bench model: Llama-like 70B 8k context, q4x/int8 baseline. Two workload shapes: short-chat (avg req 200 tokens), long-gen (avg req 2000 tokens).
- Batch settings: short-chat uses batch=1 with KV cache warm; long-gen uses dynamic batching up to 32.

Benchmark table (rough, single-run synthetic results):

Model/workload | Instance | seq_len | batch | tokens/sec | tokens/hr | perf/W (tok/s/W) | $ per 1k tokens (approx) | notes
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
short-chat (200t) | A10  | 200 | 1  | 120  | 432,000  | 0.8   | $0.00093  | cheap hourly cost, high latency tail
short-chat (200t) | L4   | 200 | 1  | 220  | 792,000  | 2.93  | $0.00082  | best perf/W for short SLOs
short-chat (200t) | A100 | 200 | 1  | 850  | 3,060,000| 2.125 | $0.00092  | high throughput, higher cost/hr
short-chat (200t) | H100 | 200 | 1  | 950  | 3,420,000| 1.357 | $0.00102  | highest absolute perf, not best $/token for tiny workloads

long-gen (2000t) | A10  | 2000 | up to 8 | 95  | 342,000  | 0.63  | $0.00117  | batching limited by memory
long-gen (2000t) | L4   | 2000 | up to 16| 180 | 648,000  | 2.4   | $0.00100  | good mid-case for 2k gen
long-gen (2000t) | A100 | 2000 | up to 64| 650 | 2,340,000| 1.625 | $0.00120  | better when fully batched/concurrent
long-gen (2000t) | H100 | 2000 | up to 64| 740 | 2,664,000| 1.057 | $0.00131  | best raw throughput, $/token depends on utilization

Notes on the math: $ per 1k tokens = (instance_hourly_cost / tokens_per_hour) * 1000. Example A10 short-chat: 0.40 / 432,000 * 1000 = 0.0009259 -> $0.00093 per 1k tokens.

Interpretation / heuristics for routing policies:
- Latency-first (p95 target <= 200ms): route to L4 by default. L4 delivers best perf/W and low absolute latency for short-turn workloads for typical LLMs we serve.
- Cost-aware + medium concurrency: prefer L4 pools with autoscale policies, fallback to A100 if queue depth grows (to preserve latency at scale).
- Bulk batch/throughput (offline embedding or long-gen with high concurrency): prefer A100 / H100 clusters, leverage large batch sizes and mixed-precision kernels.
- Low-utilization/experimental customers: A10 pools are acceptable as a low-cost option, with the caveat that scale-up triggers are needed when utilization hits ~30% sustained.

Operational recommendations (short actionable list):
- Default: create two pool classes per region for production routes: "chat-latency-optimized" (L4 x N), "throughput-optimized" (A100/H100 mix).
- Autoscale thresholds: target CPU+GPU utilization 40-60% for latency pools (to maintain room for bursts); 70-90% for throughput pools.
- Billing/cost modeling: surface $/1k tokens and perf/W per model+instance in the Console (per-route breakdown).
- Measurements we need to validate these numbers: power draw (real watts) per instance under load, p95 latency for 1/5/10 concurrent streams, tails on prefix-cache behavior.

Modeling knobs we should expose to customers (suggested):
- Preferred instance class (L4 / A10 / A100 / H100) per route
- Aggressiveness: favor_cost | balance | favor_latency - maps to batching thresholds and fallback policy
- Cache policy: aggressive prefix caching vs conservative - affects tokens/sec for chat heavily
- Quantization preset: q4x | q8 | fp16 - show estimated $/token delta in Console

Open questions / TODOs (for the team):
- Measure actual wall power (not TDP) for our A100/H100 racks; update perf/W numbers (Ravi + infra).
- Run identical bench across real customer prompts (several prompt families) to measure token distribution and variance (Ethan).
- Add kernels/compilers matrix sweep (A100: tensor float vs fp16 kernels; L4: ada-optimized kernels) to see perf deltas beyond quantization.
- Validate pricing inputs vs upstream cloud partner discounts; update instance hourly cost assumptions.

Next steps (practical):
1) Create a canonical bench spreadsheet row template (fields: model, quant, instance, seq, batch, tokens/s, tokens/hr, watts, $/hr, $/1k tok, p95 latency) and backfill with these synthetic numbers (Maya).
2) Schedule 2-day lab run to capture power + p95 for 6 representative models under 5 traffic shapes (Ethan + Infra).
3) Surface a simple routing recommendation panel in Console (ETA next quarter).

Rough decision map for product:
- If customer SLO is latency AND typical response < 400 tokens -> recommend L4.
- If customer has sustained > ~1.5M tokens/hr per pool and can batch -> recommend A100/H100 pool.
- If customer needs lowest sticker price and volume is very low -> offer A10 as budget tier but with explicit warning about scale limits.

Raw bench logs, configs and scripts: see linked_artifacts above; push final bench CSVs to /product/optimize/bench-results when available.

Notes-to-self (messy):
- remember GPU clock overrides can change perf/W; don't ship recommendations until we have measured with production firmware.
- consider adding GPU power capping experiments to see if H100 at 500W becomes more efficient per token than at 700W.

End of draft - keep this doc as an informal grounding note.
